title: Grateful Dead Live at Pauley Pavilion, UCLA on 1982-02-21
lineage: Sbd> cassette > dat> cdr> Eac > cool edit pro > shntool > cdwav > shnv3

ai_review.summary: Soundboard capture of a high‑energy early‑80s Dead show with scorching Shakedown, Bird Song and a tight Bertha > Women Smarter, though a flat mix and the missing China Cat keep it from being perfect.
ai_review.review: The performance is a classic early‑'80s set that bursts with excitement – Jerry tears into “Shakedown,” Brent delivers memorable keyboard solos, Phil drops bass bombs on the NFA→Stella sequence, and Bob’s rhythm work shines throughout. The soundboard source is generally clear and well‑mixed, but listeners note a slightly flat tonal balance and the absence of the China Cat Sunflower track, which leaves a small gap in an otherwise solid recording.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4‑5 stars and praise the show’s energy and musicianship; recording comments are largely favorable with minor flatness issues, yielding a strong overall score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear and listenable soundboard mix, though several reviewers describe the tonal balance as a bit flat and wish for more bass presence. No major drop‑outs reported.

poor_songs: China Cat Sunflower (missing from this version)
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set builds strong momentum with Shakedown and Bird Song, leading into a powerful Bertha > Women Smarter closing. Second set stays tight, highlighted by the NFA→Stella sequence and a solid encore, though the missing China Cat leaves a small gap.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Rips into Shakedown with fire; guitar tone praised as ‘on fire’ and tight throughout.
band_member_comments.Phil: Drops bass bombs on the NFA→Stella section, delivering sweet, fast‑paced lines that stand out.
band_member_comments.Bob: Great rhythm guitar tone noted; energetic playing described as a “walking encyclopedia of broken chords” with strong presence.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent’s solos are highlighted as memorable and engaging; overall keyboard work is solid though some wish for more bass balance.
